label: Flight controller
title: Flight Controller Board
body: The satellite's main computer. It runs the flight software, talks to the ground through the radio, and decides which subsystems get power. In this model it is a simplified placeholder shape.

label: Battery board
title: Battery Board
body: Holds the lithium-ion cells and the power electronics (EPS) that charge them from the solar panels and hand out regulated power. V3 and later boards carry their own RP2040 microcontroller.

label: Card brackets
title: Card Brackets
body: Long aluminium angle brackets that screw to two edges of a board and then to the frame. Only the battery board's pair is a separate part in this model. The flight controller and payload brackets are not modeled yet.

label: Payload slot
title: Payload Slot
body: The open slot in the middle of the stack, where a mission's payload board goes. Electra's design filled it with a lead block that raised the satellite's mass to almost 2 kg. A heavier satellite loses speed to atmospheric drag more slowly, so it stays in orbit longer. The block was designed and built, but Electra flew without it.

label: Solar X+
title: XY Solar Panel (X+)
body: One of four side panels. Its solar cells charge the battery, and its sensors (sun, temperature) and magnetorquer coil help the satellite know and change its orientation. The X and Y labels are for reference only. You choose the satellite's body frame when you configure the flight software.

label: Solar X−
title: XY Solar Panel (X−)
body: One of four side panels. Its solar cells charge the battery, and its sensors (sun, temperature) and magnetorquer coil help the satellite know and change its orientation. The X and Y labels are for reference only. You choose the satellite's body frame when you configure the flight software.

label: Solar Y+
title: XY Solar Panel (Y+)
body: One of four side panels, identical to the others. The X and Y labels are for reference only. You choose the satellite's body frame when you configure the flight software.

label: Solar Y−
title: XY Solar Panel (Y−)
body: One of four side panels, identical to the others. The X and Y labels are for reference only. You choose the satellite's body frame when you configure the flight software.

label: Solar Z−
title: Z− Solar Panel
body: The bottom face. Six small solar cells plus a temperature sensor, a light sensor and a haptic motor driver, wired to the stack over one 5-pin connector.

label: Antenna board Z+
title: Antenna Board (Z+)
body: The top cap. It holds the stowed antennas down until the satellite is in orbit, then burns them free. One Berkley FireLine fishing line ties to the end of one antenna, loops once around the burn resistor on this board, and ties to the end of the other. Heating the resistor melts the line in the middle. The spring steel flings both antennas out, and each half of the line stays tied to its antenna, so nothing is ejected.

label: Antenna elements
title: Antenna Elements
body: Two lengths of steel tape measure that form a dipole. Each is cut to about 165 mm for the 437 MHz amateur band. In this model they are stowed: the yellow strips wrapped around the kit.

label: Frame half A
title: 1U Structure (half A)
body: The frame is two identical sheet-metal halves bolted together. It sets the 10 cm cube shape that fits the deployer, and every board mounts to it.

label: Frame half B
title: 1U Structure (half B)
body: The second of the two identical frame halves. Splitting the frame in half makes it cheap to cut and easy to open for integration.

label: Feet
title: Feet
body: The corner feet are the only parts that touch the deployer rails. The deployment switches go on the top feet, at the antenna board end, so the kit turns on while standing upright on the bench.

label: L-brackets
title: L-Brackets
body: Four small elbow brackets with press-in (PEM) nuts that join the two frame halves at their seam. Fasten them with M2.5x5 button head screws, not pan heads, so the solar faces sit flat over the screw heads.

label: Fasteners
title: Fasteners
body: M2.5 screws and nuts that hold the kit together.
